title: A guardian and a child, without joining them into one record
summary: Sub-accounts link two people who are still two people: each keeps their own pseudonym, their own blob and their own rights. The link says how they relate, inside one scope, and it dies when either of them is erased.

steps.label: The guardian
steps.note: An ordinary person record - nothing about them says 'parent' yet.

steps.label: The child, as their own person
steps.note: Deliberately NOT a field on the guardian's record. A child who becomes an adult must be able to keep their data and lose the link - which is impossible if they were only ever an attribute of someone else.

assert.message: guardian and child must be separate people with separate pseudonyms

steps.label: A link with a stated type
steps.note: guardian, member or owner - the relationship is named, not implied. Both ends must be in the caller's own scope: a link can never cross a scope boundary, or it would become the cross-system join key the whole design removes.

steps.label: A made-up relationship is refused
steps.note: The vocabulary is closed. 'overlord' is not a relationship the system can reason about, so it is not one it will store.

steps.label: List the guardian's links
steps.note: Each entry is the OTHER end's pseudonym in this scope, plus the type and the direction. This read is audited like every other read of a person.

steps.label: Erase the child
steps.note: One of the two people exercises Article 17. The other is untouched - that is the point of keeping them separate.

steps.label: The link went with them
steps.note: A surviving link would keep leaking the erased person's pseudonym through the guardian's listing - and, once the child is a tombstone, nobody could remove it through the API any more. So erasure deletes links at both ends.

steps.label: The guardian is still here
steps.note: Erasing one person does not touch the other. Cascading to children is possible, but only when the caller asks for it explicitly.
